ev.q: Although most (93.5%) women received syphilis screening during pregnancy, 26.8% were not screened sufficiently early to prevent adverse pregnancy outcomes.
Many women were not screened for HIV infection (31.1%), chlamydia (25.3%), or gonorrhea (25.7%).
Although most (93.5%) women received syphilis screening during pregnancy, 26.8% were not screened sufficiently early to prevent adverse pregnancy outcomes.
Women who began prenatal care in their third trimester had 5.6 times the prevalence of late or no syphilis screening
After adjusting for all nine screening correlates, late prenatal care and low number of prenatal care visits were significantly associated
Data came from the medical records of a randomly selected sample of mothers with live births in 2014

methods_quotes.q: Bivariate analyses and multivariable models using Poisson regression were conducted to determine factors associated with inadequate screening for syphilis and other STIs.
Separate Poisson regression models provided unadjusted and adjusted prevalence ratios (APR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs)
All nine potential correlates of screening were included in the multivariable Poisson regression models for fully adjusted estimates.
Restricted to records with no missing information on HIV screening (n = 842).
